"''Looks like you're right about that, sir!|Kit Fisto and Commander Fil, upon seeing Gor|audio=WorseThingsThanGrievous-LoG.flac|}} '''Gor''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Roggwart/Legends|roggwart]] owned by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Grievous, who served as the [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]' [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]], kept Gor in [[Grievous's castle/Legends|his castle]] on the [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third moon]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vassek/Legends|Vassek]]. There, Gor acted as both a guard and a pet for the general, and was one of the few creatures Grievous cared for. While the general was away, Gor was tended to by his master's [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droid]], [[EV-A4-D/Legends|EV-A4-D]]. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was responsible for fitting Gor with four [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic limbs]] grafted to his back, and attaching an exoskeleton of [[Armor/Legends|armor]] to the roggwart's body. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Confederate [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]], [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], lured a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-led [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] task force to Grievous's castle in an attempt to test the general's skills. Grievous ordered Gor to [[Death/Legends|kill]] the intruders, but the roggwart was slain by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]]. ==Biography== ===Early life=== {{Quote|Gor, time to entertain our guests!|General Grievous|audio=GorTimeToEntertain-LoG.flac|}} Following the defeat of the [[Bitthævrian/Legends|Bitthævrians]] in the [[Bitthævrian War]], the victorious [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] warlords took [[Roggwart/Legends|roggwarts]] as trophies from the Bitthævrian homeworld of [[Guiteica/Legends|Guiteica]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1]]'' One such roggwart came into the possession of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], who named it "Gor." During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Grievous kept Gor within his [[Grievous's castle/Legends|castle]] on the [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third moon]] of [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Vassek/Legends|Vassek]]. Trained to keep watch, Gor served as a guard alongside Grievous's [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuard]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], and came to be loved by the general. Despite Grievous's affection for his pet, the cyborg understood that Gor's abilities as the castle guardian could be enhanced through the use of [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]], just as similar technology had improved Grievous's abilities. To that end, the general ordered his caretaker and [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droid]], [[EV-A4-D/Legends|EV-A4-D]], to attach four mechanical arms to Gor's back, and to graft exoskeletal [[Armor/Legends|armor]] to the beast's body. A chest plate was included to protect his vital organs, while the helmet to protect his brain case. ===Involvement in the Clone Wars=== ====Guarding Grievous==== In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] member [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] [[Rescue on the Tranquility/Legends|escaped]] from [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] captivity while aboard the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Tranquility/Legends|''Tranquility'']] and fled in a stolen [[Consular-class cruiser (Charger c70 retrofit)/Legends|Republic frigate]]. Intending to reassess Grievous's abilities after the general was defeated numerous times in battle, Confederate [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] sent the [[Frigate/Legends|frigate's]] [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking beacon]] to Grievous's castle in order to lure Republic forces there. While the general was away from the castle, Dooku remotely deactivated his MagnaGuards, leaving no one to feed Gor. The roggwart was shrieking in hunger by the time Republic forces arrived to search the castle for Gunray. [[File:GorDeath-LairOfGrievous.png|thumb|left|230px|Gor's death at the hands of Kit Fisto]] [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]], and a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] under the command of [[Clone Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Fil/Legends|Fil]] [[Mission to Grievous's castle/Legends|infiltrated]] the castle shortly before Grievous returned. Upon his arrival, the general was badly damaged by the Republic and Jedi forces and retreated deep into his castle to be repaired by EV-A4-D. Before beginning his repairs, Grievous released Gor into the corridors of the castle to hunt down the intruders. The roggwart found Fisto, Vebb, and Fil in one of the castle's large rooms and attacked them. Fil fired on Gor several times, but its tough hide and armor rendered the [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] shots ineffective. An aggravated Gor lunged at Fisto, disarming the [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] Jedi Master. ====Final showdown and death==== As the three intruders surrounded Gor, Fil continued to shoot at the roggwart's neck. Vebb drove his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] into the creature's back, which did little to slow Gor, who quickly bucked Vebb off and grabbed Fil with his prehensile tail, flailing the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] about. Vebb again approached Gor and was again beaten back, this time by the creature's tail that held Fil. Fisto, who had regained his lightsaber, sliced at Gor's face, causing the roggwart to slam Fil into the ground. Vebb rushed forward again, this time slicing off Gor's tail and freeing Fil, who perished from his wounds. Fisto also attacked Gor, who had been distracted by the loss of his tail, slicing off the creature's two front limbs. Gor fell to the ground in pain and was quickly killed by Fisto via a lightsaber stab to the throat. When Grievous's repairs were completed, the general attempted to see if Gor had finished "playing" with the Jedi, only to discover that Gor had been slain—a revelation that greatly upset the general. ==Personality and traits== [[File:Roggwart.png|thumb|right|220px|Gor in Grievous's castle]] {{Quote|Well ''that'' was something.|A clone trooper, upon hearing Gor in Grievous's seemingly empty castle|audio=WellThatWasSomething-LoG.flac|}} Gor was a male roggwart—a large, predatory, [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] beast. At a height of 4.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] and a weight of 254 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]], he had large, sharp teeth and two horns that curved downward from his head. Gor's long tail ended in three prehensile graspers that were capable of impaling foes, and his hands and feet both ended in large claws. His muscular body was capable of withstanding blaster shots and enduring modest lightsaber wounds. Additionally, he had a long, gooey projectile tongue.{{CSWECite|III||Roggwart}} Gor was fitted with a set of battle armor and four large mechanical arms that extended from his back; the chest plate was included to protect his vital organs, while the helmet was created to protect his brain case.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.24|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.24]] He screeched loudly when hungry. Gor had an aggressive disposition, which was evident during his battle with the Jedi. Given his position as a guard in Grievous's castle, Gor was likely taken from his [[brood-nest]] early in life; only roggwarts taken at a such a young age were able to be trained as watch-guardians or pets. The general himself was fond of Gor, doting on the roggwart during his time in the castle. Grievous indeed identified with the creature, and eventually noted that Gor would benefit from a cybernetic transformation just as he had earlier in his life. Upon discovering his pet's death, Grievous was enraged, and added that offense to an already lengthy list of wrongs the general believed the Jedi Order had committed. ==Behind the scenes== Gor was created for the [[2008]] ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series. Gor was first mentioned in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]'' as the first depiction of the roggwart [[Species/Legends|species]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]'' He later made his series debut in the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|season one]] episode "[[Lair of Grievous]]." Gor's voice was created from sounds of a lion and a vulture.{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-present-familiar-creatures-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}} The spelling of Gor's name is disputed by several differing sources. While most sources, including the ''Visual Guide'', claim that it is spelled "Gor," ''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' spells it as "Gore."''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' The episode guide also refers to him once as "Gorr." While [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1|''The Official Episode Guide: Season 1'']] claims that Gor's species originated on [[Guiteica/Legends|Guiteica]], the [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook|''Star Wars Roleplaying Game'']] supplement ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' states that they are from [[Vendaxa/Legends|Vendaxa]] instead.''[[Galaxy at War]]'' In [[2010]], Gor's homeworld was officially stated to be Guiteica with the release of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''. ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' lists Gor's height as 4.5 meters, while ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Head-to-Head]]'' lists it as 4.65 meters. This article assumes that the former source is correct. ===Non-canon history=== ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Head-to-Head'' presents a non-canon matchup involving Gor, pitting him against the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] warrior [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]. When Chewbacca becomes trapped inside Grievous's lair on the third [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of Vassek, Gor blocks his escape. However, Chewbacca confronts him directly, and Gor, being unaccustomed to his prey running toward him, fails to prevent the Wookiee from severing his cybernetic limbs. Chewbacca is thus able to trap Gor in a nerve-pinning headlock, causing the roggwart to fall unconscious. ===Concept art gallery=== {{Gallery |source=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' |storyboards= |concept= File:GorConcept-TCW.png|Concept design by [[Atsushi Takeuchi|A.
